title: Settlement Desk Guidance: Withdrawing a Settlement Agreements Offer or Accepted Settlement
content:
# Settlement Agreements — Withdrawal

Ridgeline withdraws an offered or accepted settlement under its Settlement Agreements only for a reason shown on the account's own records — account disputed when the account entered dispute hold, account returned when the account was returned to the client, bankruptcy notice or consumer deceased when the matching protected-status notice is recorded, and superseded by new offer for an offer that is still only offered when the consumer asks for different terms.

## Reasons and the record each rests on

| Withdrawal reason | Record that must show it | Settlement it may be used on |
|---|---|---|
| account disputed | the account entered dispute hold | offered or accepted |
| account returned | the account was returned to the client | offered or accepted |
| bankruptcy notice | a bankruptcy protected-status notice is recorded on the account | offered or accepted |
| consumer deceased | a deceased protected-status notice is recorded on the account | offered or accepted |
| superseded by new offer | the consumer asks for different terms | offered only |

## Further terms

- A consumer who simply changes their mind about an accepted settlement does not withdraw it; the settlement stays accepted until it is fulfilled or defaults.
- Withdrawing an accepted settlement releases its remaining settlement balance and returns an arranged account to active unless the account is being returned; payments already made stay applied to the account.
- When the dispute that caused an account-disputed withdrawal is later verified, the consumer may receive a new offer without waiting for the re-offer cooling-off period.

## Hypothetical cases

1. A consumer with an accepted settlement in good standing says they no longer want it. No withdrawal reason is shown on the records; the settlement stays accepted.
2. An accepted settlement on an account that has just entered dispute hold is withdrawn as account disputed; its remaining settlement balance is released and the arranged account returns to active.
3. An accepted settlement on an account being returned to the client is withdrawn as account returned; its remaining settlement balance is released, and the account does not return to active.
